geo:places-nw.summary:
I wrote real coordinates for all 296 north and west ids in /home/user/DS/nostalgia/design/geo/places_nw.json, and their GHMC wards in places_nw_wards.json. The 296 are 252 places from N.WORLD_DATA.places plus 44 landmark ids that have no place entry. Only 21 coordinates are high confidence, 63 are medium and 212 are low; nearly all the low ones are everyday places and decorations. Every entry has lat, lon, confidence, source and note, and the two files cover the same ids. Every point was checked against the ward polygons with a script: 271 fall inside a ward and 25 fall outside all wards, each labelled with the reason and the nearest ward. A second script confirmed that no point sits in water, except the Buddha statue, which correctly lands on its OSM island.

**Which ids I took.** Every place in the districts hitec, erragadda, begumpet, secunderabad, marredpally, ameerpet, hussain_sagar, jubilee, banjara, khairatabad, musheerabad, osmania, golconda, tolichowki, masab_tank, langar_houz and rajendranagar (that last one holds Golconda, Taramati and the western edge signposts). I also took 10 places the map files under basheerbagh that are really at Lakdikapul, Saifabad or Naubat Pahad, including Birla Mandir, the Secretariat, Niloufer cafe, Ravindra Bharathi and All India Radio. Plus the 44 landmark-only ids in those districts (Tank Bund statues, Qutb tombs, Golconda walls, rail halts, coaching centres and so on), except jubilee_hall. I did not cover Himayatnagar, so the player's colony (home, the terraces, playground_1) has no anchor from me. I also left out Public Gardens, the Assembly, LB Stadium and the zoo, except hide_zoo_pond, which the map files under langar_houz.

**High-confidence entries (21)** come from map data or from several sources that agree: Buddha statue, Hussain Sagar, Tank Bund, Durgam Cheruvu, Lumbini Park, Prasads IMAX, Birla Mandir, the Secretariat, Lakdikapul, Panjagutta, NIMS, Secunderabad station, Clock Tower, Monda Market, James Street and Sanjeevaiah Park halts, Begumpet station, Hyderabad Public School, Shilparamam, Gachibowli stadium and the Qutb Shahi Tombs.

**Medium entries (63)** rest on one source or a well-known fact, often a Wikipedia coordinate read through search summaries. These include Paradise, Ujjaini Mahankali, Golconda, Osmania University Arts College, Tarnaka, Jubilee Hills Check Post, KBR Park, Raj Bhavan and the Khairatabad Ganesh site.

**Low entries (212)** are estimates. Everyday places (kirana, cafes, carts, bus stops, hide spots, schools) sit in the same neighbourhood they serve in the current map, positioned around a known junction and checked against the ward. Individual Tank Bund statues, single Qutb tombs and the Golconda wall pieces are also low.

**Things the merge needs to handle:**
- Seven ids lie north of the world's top edge (17.475N): kphb_colony, playground_16, playground_kit_16, jntu_kukatpally, holy_trinity_church_bolarum, church_holy_trinity and rashtrapati_nilayam. university_of_hyderabad (the gate) is just west of the world's west edge, at 78.3345E.
- The four western edge signposts (gandipet, chilkur_balaji, mrugavani_park, himayat_sagar) are placed at the world edge. Their real destinations, given in each note, are outside the world.
- The 25 points outside all wards are Cantonment ground (Parade Grounds, Marredpally, Gymkhana, Secunderabad Club, Bolarum), Begumpet airport land, the Osmania University campus (a gap in the ward map) and the edge signposts.
- Some real layouts differ from the current map. Monda Market is west of Secunderabad station, not north-east. Shilparamam is west of Cyber Towers, not east. Sanjeevaiah Park is a peninsula on the lake's north shore, not far to the north.
- Some places fall in surprising wards. The ward map puts Golconda Fort in Ward 66 Langar Houz, 254 m from Ward 67 Golconda, while every coordinate source places the fort here. KBR Park lands in Ward 92 Venkateshwara Colony and Birla Mandir in Ward 78 Gunfoundry.
- golconda_fort marks the entrance gate, about 330 m east of the hilltop. golconda_bala_hissar uses the standard fort coordinate.
- Wikipedia values I rejected as wrong: Sanjeevaiah Park (it points to Koti), Tolichowki (points to Karwan), Punjagutta metro, Jubilee Hills Check Post (that is the locality centre), NTR Gardens (copy of the Lumbini value) and Moula Ali hill. I used the OSM metro line positions, the points where three ward boundaries meet, or other listings instead.

**Sources and credits.** Ward boundaries are DataMeet Municipal Spatial Data (CC BY 4.0, derived from OSM, ODbL). I cloned a second open repo, Lakeer-org/hyderabad-open-gis-data, to /home/user/lakeer-org/hyderabad-open-gis-data and used only its OpenStreetMap-derived layers (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL): railways (MMTS and the metro lines that run along the main roads), lakes and rivers. Its other layers have no stated licence, so I did not use them. The credits need "© OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)" for those layers too, which the required A1 credit line already covers. The rest came from Wikipedia coordinates and a few listing or directory sites, each named in the entry's source field. The OSM railway and waterway layers would also help whoever lays the real road and water alignments.
notes: Confidence counts: high 21, medium 63, low 212 (296 ids). The 44 landmark-only ids split 3 high, 3 medium, 38 low.

Confidence rule: high means map data, or two or more agreeing coordinate sources, or a single source that independently matched my prior knowledge within about 50 m. One coordinate source means medium. Estimates are low. Wikipedia-only coordinates that did not match my prior knowledge were set to medium.

Each JSON file is a flat {placeId: ...} object with no extra metadata key, so a merge script can iterate it directly. A ward value is either a ward name or a string starting with 'outside GHMC wards: <reason> (nearest Ward X, N m)'.

The two Tank Bund end points come from the OSM lake edge pushed 25 m outward. The 12 statues are spaced evenly between them, and the carts and bus stop on the bund are moved 10-15 m onto the outer footpath so they do not sit on a statue.
Alias ids get the same coordinates as their main id: irani_cafe_4/5/6/17/18, mosque_9, bonalu, ganesh_immersion, lumbini_boat, church_st_johns, church_holy_trinity, jubilee_hills_check_post.

The scratchpad is shared with other agents: my first scope.json and wd.json there were overwritten. All my working files are now in scratchpad/nwgeo/. Running dump.cjs, then build_nw.py, then write_nw.py regenerates both outputs.
known_issues: Wikipedia coordinates were read through search-result summaries, not the live infoboxes (Wikipedia is blocked here), so a few summary values may be mirrors or slightly stale.

Several important places have only a low or medium position because no coordinate source was reachable: Sangeet X Roads and its theatres, St John's Church, Secunderabad Club, Moula Ali Dargah, Rashtrapati Nilayam, Hussain Shah Wali Dargah, Annapurna and Ramanaidu Studios, Niloufer cafe, All India Radio, Hill Fort Palace, the Golconda gates and walls, Katta Maisamma, Ranigunj, General Bazaar and Chenoy Trade Centre.
The Kakatiya arches at both ends of the Tank Bund are game decoration. I found no real arch there, so they are pinned to the bund ends as low confidence.

GHMC ward boundaries come from OpenStreetMap in 2017-18 and are approximate. Places within about 50 m of a boundary may report the neighbouring ward, for example Erragadda junction, which reports Sanath Nagar.

Everyday places are kept in their neighbourhood and ward, but no street layer was available, so they are not snapped to a specific street. Only the arterials can be checked, against the OSM metro and rail lines.
The player's colony and terrace anchors in Himayatnagar are outside this north-west area and were not produced here.

traffic+wanted.summary:
City life and the Chappal Meter are installed. src/traffic.js (2695 lines) and src/wanted.js (1779 lines) replace the stubs; nobody else had written real code there, so nothing needed merging. Their staging copies are byte-identical, and index.html already loads both. The orchestrator's WIP commit e3d41e2 already includes them and tests/traffic.cjs.

traffic.js: ambient vehicles drive on the LEFT along the road graph, with lane offsets. They follow the car ahead, give way at junctions (podium signals and box occupancy), honk with a shared budget, swerve round cows and people, and react to the player's horn. Autos drop passengers and buses stop 4 s at bus stops on their side of the road. The vehicle mix depends on the district: autos and buses everywhere, cycles and Lunas in colonies, Ambassadors and Padminis near offices, RX100s, lorries on arterials, cycle-rickshaws in the old city, boats on Hussain Sagar. Off-screen vehicles switch to a cheap mode. Pedestrians walk the footpaths, cross at junction mouths and sometimes jaywalk. Their clothes fit the district: burqas, skull caps and Friday sherwanis in the old city, aunties in sarees, lungi uncles, school kids in uniform during school hours, students at Osmania, office workers at HITEC. They crowd bus stands, stations, cinemas (show times), temples, mosques, markets, Gokul Chat, Irani cafes, schools and playgrounds. Vendors push carts, and balloon sellers appear in parks at dusk. People jump aside, get knocked down and get up, and bark Hyderabadi lines. Seasonal events are handled (Numaish, Ramzan, Ganesh idol lorries, Bonalu, Thursday Sai temple, Sankranti, Chand Raat). Animals: cows lie on roads, dogs chase cyclists and roam in packs at night (they can be fed), goats graze in the old city, and pigeons at Charminar and other squares scatter. Caps: 28 vehicles and 45 peds on desktop, 20 and 32 on touch.

vehicles-v2.summary:
I've implemented A2 (potholes) and A3 (age-appropriate vehicles) in the files I own. tests/vehicles_v2.cjs passes all 105 checks, and smoke.cjs and shops.cjs both pass. collectibles.cjs and traffic.cjs also still pass. core_systems.cjs fails before it reaches any vehicle code: clicking #title-start now plays the prologue cutscene, so it never reaches 'play' (from other agents' story work). N.world.potholeAt does not exist yet, so the pothole checks use a stub; real potholes have not been exercised.

**New vehicle types (src/vehicles.js)**
- **hero_cycle** ("Ride Hero cycle"): black roadster, top 110 u/s, heavy and steady, weaker rod brakes. Art shows the rod brakes, rear carrier (NPC riders sometimes carry a tiffin or a bundle), chain guard with gold pinstripe, black mudguards with the white tail and red reflector, sprung saddle, swept bar, bell and a dynamo lamp that only glows while moving. Chinnu rides it kainchi style, standing beside the frame.
- **hercules_cycle** ("Ride Hercules"): bright frame with a decal band, fat knobbly tyres, flat bar. Top 120, quicker, turns sharper, keeps more speed on dirt, gets half as many punctures and less pothole speed loss.
- **hercules_gears**: the geared Hercules, top 132.
- **scooty** ("Ride Scooty"): small bright step-through scooter with mirrors and a headlamp. Top 122, light, worse off-road. Chinnu perches on the front of the seat, arms straight, toes reaching for the floorboard. Above 78% of top speed the handlebar wobbles (`v.wobble`).
- **akka_scooty**: Akka's Scooty, parked at home.
- `cycle` is now named "BSA SLR cycle" and there is a `bsa_cycle` alias. `ladiescycle` (now labelled "Ride ladies cycle") and `kid_cycle` use the new cycle art.
- Every type now has spawn weights per district style.

Measured with real keys (top speed / 0-80 u/s): Hero 110 / 1.67 s, Hercules 120 / 1.30 s, Scooty 123 with the wobble, auto with Chinnu 108 of 135.

**Age rules**
- Chinnu may drive only `kidOk` types: all cycles, both Scooties and the auto.
- **Parked disallowed types** (Luna, Chetak, family Chetak, RX100, cars, bus, lorry, boats): the label is "Too small to drive" and ACTION toasts a kid line ("Nanna will kill me if I touch his Chetak!", "Feet don't even reach, baba"). The family Chetak and Bunty's RX100 are pillion-only now.
- **Vehicles with an NPC driver:**
  - "Sit pillion" / "Ride as passenger" for Nanna, Bunty and story NPCs.
  - "Ask for a lift" on a stranger's two-wheeler.
  - "Board bus ₹3"; boarding a moving bus is the footboard scolding plus heat.
  - "Ride auto (fare)" for working traffic autos, through shops.
  - A stranger's car politely refuses.
- **Riding along:** `N.vehicles.ride()` puts Chinnu on the vehicle while the driver's own controller keeps driving. ACTION "Ask to stop" makes the driver brake and lets him off.
- **Debug:** `N.vehicles.allowHeavy`, `ageRules = false` and `N.debug.enterVehicle` still drive anything. After a load, a save made at the wheel of a disallowed type drops him off safely.
- **Kid in an auto:** top speed ×0.8. His head peeks out under the canopy and autowalas shout at him in speech bubbles.

**Traffic and parking**
- Vehicles.js patches `N.traffic.TUNE.mix` once, splitting the cycle share Hero 45% / Hercules 25% / BSA 30% and adding the Scooty. Live traffic now shows them.
- Scooty riders are restyled to women and college girls, Hercules riders to students.
- About 40 cycles and Scooties are parked at schools, cinemas, cafés, kiranas, OU and Ameerpet.
- Hire stalls now have kid, Hero, Hercules and ladies cycles.

**Potholes**
- For each moving vehicle near the view, plus the player's always, the front and rear wheels are checked against `N.world.potholeAt`. If the function is missing, nothing happens.
- On entry: speed ×0.82 at full depth and top speed, `v.jolt` = 1 (the 2D body drops, bounces and wiggles), a 1.5 camera shake and the 'pothole' sound (louder with speed) for the player. Dust when dry; muddy drops and the wet sound variant after rain.
- Over 6000 trials: 3.8% punctures on cycles (target 4%), 1.7% comic falls above 80% of top speed (target 2%), none below.
- Walking through one is a tiny stumble, with a splash if wet.

**Unlock ladder (collectibles.js)**
- 30 finds is now "Akka's Scooty". It sets both `unlock_scooty` and `unlock_chetak`, and old saves with only `unlock_chetak` also get `unlock_scooty`.
- 60 finds is now pillion rides with Bunty-anna plus his Hercules with gears, parked at home. It sets `unlock_rx100`, `unlock_bunty_pillion` and `unlock_hercules_gears`. Rewards appear at home as soon as they unlock.

**Shops**
- Cycle hire offers kid / big black Hero / Hercules / ladies; the Hercules costs ₹4 an hour (cap ₹12).
- New STD row "Call Bunty-anna": weekdays 16:00–21:30, Sundays from 09:00, once a day, refused at Chappal Meter ≥ 3.
- "Pillion with Bunty-anna" is offered at chai_bandi_3 (11:00–16:00) and ameerpet_coaching (18:00–21:00).
- `N.shops.rideVehicle(v)` claims a traffic auto or taxi and opens the fare card.

**Audio**
- New Scooty engine: a thin, high 2-stroke buzz, above the Chetak.
- Engine and horn now follow each type's base vehicle, so story types sound right.
- Hero bell (big double-dome trring) and Hercules bell (bright ding-ding) are distinct.
- The Scooty horn is a higher "peep peep".
- The pothole sound has a second "dak" and a wet splash variant.

Please make it O(1) (a grid or hash) and deterministic. Return {depth, r, wet?, x?, y?} or null; return the same object for the same pothole if you can. depth <= 1 is read as a 0..1 severity; larger values are treated as world units divided by 3 (severity 1 at depth 3). A typical colony-lane pothole should be depth 0.6-1, arterials 0.3-0.5. If you omit wet, vehicles.js treats a pothole as wet when it is raining or N.flags.wet_roads / puddles is set. If the function throws, it is disabled for the session (logged as N.err 'world.potholeAt').

**A3 bypasses and broken rides (fixed in src/vehicles.js)**
- **Thrown off a pillion ride:** if the driver crashed at 90 u/s or more, Chinnu was thrown off but the NPC's Chetak was also marked as fallen. - **"Too small to drive" crowding:** it showed at priority 0 within 18 u of every parked Chetak or car. That hid side activities and the Hero cycle parked next to it, and mashing E queued up to 6 different lines.

api_notes: Coordinates: three (x, y, z) = world (x, height, y); +x east, +z south, +y up; a model facing world angle a gets rotation.y = -a (H.place(obj, x, y, h, a)). Vertical scale N.view3d.VS = 1.5: a data storey of 10u is 15u in 3D (N.view3d.FLOOR_H). People are ~7u (kids) to ~9u (adults) tall. Roof floors are at roof.h * VS (N.view3d.elevation(e)).

N.view3d.registerLandmark(drawId | '#landmarkId', build(THREE, lm, H) -> Object3D | null (generic fallback) | false (draw nothing), {castShadow, update(obj, lm, dt, H), dispose}). geo:roads-water-rail.summary:
All five geo files are written and checked in /home/user/DS/nostalgia/design/geo/. Every coordinate is a real [lat, lon] taken from open data, and each item carries a confidence and a source.

Data used:
- **Roads, water and rail (OpenStreetMap, ODbL):** taken from Overture Maps (release 2026-09-23.0, public S3 bucket, reachable from this sandbox), OSM-sourced segments only.
- **Cross-checks:** an OSM extract of Hyderabad district (github.com/shivakumar-ui-max/hyderabad-gis-map) and Lakeer's OSM-derived layers (already cloned).
- **Stations:** DataMeet railways stations (CC0).
- **Wards:** DataMeet GHMC ward polygons (CC BY 4.0).
- **Elevation:** AWS Terrain Tiles, SRTM-based (public domain).

Attribution lines are in each file's meta.

**roads.json** – 193 roads: all 176 roads in worlddata.js plus 17 real roads that were missing.
- **Confidence:** 82 high, 89 medium, 22 low.
- **How the lines were made:** each road was routed along the real OSM street geometry between real junctions, preferring the road's OSM name, then simplified to 5–60 points.
- **Post-2003 structures:** the PVNR expressway, the steel bridges and the Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge were excluded. Other flyovers were avoided wherever a road at ground level exists; an `era_note` marks the remaining cases.
- **Per road:** lanes and divided (2003 estimates), length, OSM way ids, the wards it passes through in order, a `ward_check` on 29 key roads (all pass), and a `pothole_hint` for A2 (a design suggestion, not measured).
- **Must-include list:** every item is covered; the mapping is in `meta.must_include`. That includes all ten Musi crossings (Purana Pul, Musallam Jung, Naya Pul, Salar Jung/Afzalgunj, Imlibun, Chaderghat bridge and causeway, Golnaka, Moosarambagh, Nagole).
- **Himayatnagar grid:** a separate list of 158 lanes clipped to Ward 79 (29 named high, 129 unnamed in OSM medium). These have 2–20 points each, not 5–60.

**water.json** – 70 features: 69 high, 1 low.
- 21 lakes, including Hussain Sagar (204 points) with the Gibraltar Rock / Buddha island taken from the hole in the OSM polygon, Mir Alam, Durgam Cheruvu, Saroornagar and Himayat Sagar's corner.
- 38 small tanks.
- The Musi centreline (118 points) plus the riverbed polygon from the OSM riverbank areas, and the Esi.
- Measured riverbed width is a median of 46 m in the core (range 22–290 m). The 2003 low-water channel (about 25 m) is an estimate.
- 5 named nalas, including the Golconda moat.
- Off-map arrows: Osman Sagar and Fox Sagar (high); Shamirpet (low – its position is approximate, no data was available for it); Himayat Sagar (arrow not needed – its north-east arm is inside the frame and it is in the lakes list).

**rail.json** – 7 track sections (all high), 2 junctions found from the track geometry, and 6 services.
- The services are: Secunderabad–Nampally, Secunderabad–Lingampally, Nampally–Lingampally, Secunderabad–Falaknuma via Kacheguda/Malakpet/Dabirpura, Secunderabad–Moula Ali, and Secunderabad–Bolarum.
- 33 stations: 27 high, 6 medium. Station positions use OSM platforms wherever they exist; otherwise DataMeet and the MMTS stop list where they agree.
- Metro lines were excluded.

**terrain.json**
- 15 hills (7 high, 8 medium), each with summit point, height above sea level, height above the surrounding ground, and an outline taken from the elevation data. Examples: Naubat Pahad 561 m (+49), Golconda 608 m (+95), Koh-e-Tur/Falaknuma 589 m (+66), Moula Ali 624 m (+85; the Wikipedia summary gives 614.7 m), Fakhruddin Gutta 617 m.
- 7 rock fields (6 medium, 1 low): Banjara–Jubilee, HITEC/Madhapur, Golconda–Qutb Shahi, Falaknuma, Moula Ali, Naubat Pahad, OU.
- 22 OSM rock features (high).
- An elevation grid of 61 × 81 points at 300 m spacing for 3D mode.

**districts.json** – 40 districts: 18 high (whole wards), 22 medium (wards split between districts).
- All 39 game districts are mapped to GHMC wards, plus one new district, balanagar, for wards inside the frame that the old map did not cover.
- Land with no ward is assigned too: the Cantonment, Begumpet airport, the OU campus, Mir Alam and Nagole.
- Checks: no overlaps, and only 0.04 km² of ward area inside the frame is left unassigned.
notes: File format: every point is [lat, lon] in WGS84, rounded to 5 decimals (about 1 m of resolution; OSM street centrelines themselves are accurate to roughly 2-10 m). Polygons are closed rings. Each file has a meta block with the confidence rules, counts and attribution.

Credit line required by A1: 'Map reference: DataMeet Municipal Spatial Data (CC BY 4.0) and (c) OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)'. Also credit Overture Maps Foundation for roads, water and rail, Terrain Tiles on AWS Open Data (SRTM, public domain) for elevation, and DataMeet railways (CC0) for stations.

Some game roads do not match their real namesakes, and roads.json uses the real geometry:
- banjara_rd1: the real Road No. 1 runs north-south from Panjagutta to Masab Tank. Banjara Hills Road No. 3 (Panjagutta west to Road No. 2) was added as banjara_rd3.
- secretariat_rd: follows the lake-shore road (NTR Marg) and then IMAX to Khairatabad. The real Secretariat Road was added as secretariat_saifabad_rd.
- abids_rd: follows the OSM 'Abids to MJ Market Road'. The OSM 'Mahatma Gandhi Road' is the Secunderabad one, which is mg_rd.
- musi_south_rd: follows High Court Road, Salar Jung Road and Aziz Jung Road.
- bolarum_rd: follows Wellington Road.
- tarnaka_e_rd: follows the Habsiguda-Nacharam road.
- Each of these carries a real_name and a note.

The 17 roads added (in_game false): secretariat_saifabad_rd, panjagutta_rd, banjara_rd3, banjara_rd10, kbr_jubilee_rd, chaderghat_causeway, golnaka_bridge, mgbs_bridge, narayanguda_kachiguda_rd, tolichowki_golconda_rd, moula_ali_rd, tarnaka_sec_rd, chaderghat_amberpet_rd, raja_reddy_marg, mj_afzalgunj_link, falaknuma_station_rd, purani_haveli_rd.

Ward names often differ from the locality names:
- Golconda Fort is in Ward 66 Langar Houz.
- Tolichowki X Roads is in Ward 94 Shaikpet.
- Mehdipatnam junction is in Ward 69 Nanal Nagar.
- Koti, the Assembly and LB Stadium are in Ward 78 Gunfoundry.
- Charminar and the Salar Jung Museum are in Ward 32 Patthergatti.
- The MGBS is in Ward 30 Dabeerpura.
- Uppal X Roads is in Ward 8 Habsiguda.
- LB Nagar is in Ward 12 Mansoorabad.
- Wards are split between game districts with simple latitude/longitude lines, the Musi centreline, or a band about 170 m wide round Hussain Sagar's shore. Each ward entry records its rule.
The 'wards' list on each road skips stretches shorter than 90 m, so roads that run along a ward boundary are not listed as flipping back and forth.

The generation scripts are in the scratchpad (scripts/ folder). They were not put in the repo because I do not own any other files. Run order: net_build -> build_roads (specs_main, specs_fix, specs_lanes, specs_new, specs_fix2) -> write_roads -> final_roads, then water_build -> water_write, rail_write, terrain_write, districts_write.

Era: alignments are from 2026 OSM. Dropped as post-2003: PVNR expressway, steel bridge, Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge, ORR and a hitec_raidurg link. The 13 roads whose route still uses a flyover or old rail overbridge carry an era_note: begumpet_rd (Begumpet ROB), moula_ali_rd (Lalaguda / Maula Ali ROBs), and the at-grade stand-ins dabeerpura_rd, secretariat_rd, gunfoundry_rd, mumbai_hwy, chandrayangutta_rd, old_mumbai_rd, ou_rd, nagole_n_rd, mehdipatnam_rd, mallepally_rd and lb_nagar_s_rd. MMTS halts are flagged as new in August 2003.
known_issues: Lanes and divided (median) values are 2003 estimates. Neither is in the open data; treat them as low confidence.

Colony lanes (ln_*) and some Old City lanes (Kotla Alijah, Mitti ka Sher, Shah Ali Banda east, Gulzar Houz ring, Laad Bazaar) are placed by position, because the OSM lanes there are unnamed. Confidence is medium or low as recorded on each one.

The 22 low-confidence roads are mostly approach lanes and park walks: Public Gardens walks, Indira Park walk, Birla Mandir steps, Lumbini lane, Golconda steps, Bapu Ghat road, HPS lane, Secunderabad Club lane, airport approach, Raidurg road (era uncertain), UoH road, Falaknuma station road, Tolichowki colony lanes, and the Musheerabad link.
Durgam Cheruvu and the HITEC roads come from 2026 OSM. The 2003 HITEC road layout was sparser, so raidurg_rd and hitec_n_rd may not have existed in exactly this form.

Musi: the riverbed is today's OSM riverbank area. The 2003 dry-season channel width (about 25 m, range 10-40 m) is an estimate. The riverbed polygon only covers from about 78.40 E eastward; there are no riverbank polygons west of Langar Houz.
Shamirpet Lake's off-map target is approximate (low confidence); no open data for it could be loaded.

Elevation is SRTM-based: summits are good to about ±10 m and hill outlines are generalised. Rock-field polygons mark high rocky ground taken from the elevation data, not individual boulders. The OU rock field is low confidence.
Two hill names are uncertain: the Moula Ali south summit as Qadam-e-Rasool (low), and malkajgiri_hill, which has no name in the data.

The Cantonment and Begumpet airport land have no GHMC wards. Their split between the begumpet, secunderabad and marredpally districts uses straight lines of longitude (78.4775 and 78.495), not real boundaries.
Malkajgiri station: the two sources disagree by 839 m. The MMTS-list position, which lies on the Bolarum line, was used (medium). Five other stations without OSM platforms are also medium.
The DataMeet ward layer is missing wards 3, 4, 11 (Nagole), 13 and 113. Nagole is covered by a gap polygon in lb_nagar.

projection.summary:
I built the projection, but I chose a 15000 x 11250 u world (1.6 m per unit) instead of the 12000 x 9000 target. At 12000 x 9000 the dense cores cannot get enough room while compass bearings stay within ~15°. The frame is still the A1 frame (lon 78.33507-78.56093 E, lat 17.31218-17.47482 N, 24 x 18 km), and one constant in core.js (owned by the engine team) sets the size. All checks pass at 15000 x 11250 and every preview is rendered and reviewed.

**Why not 12000 x 9000.** The cores (Charminar, Abids, Himayatnagar, Tank Bund, Secunderabad) lie in one north-south band about 10 km long inside an 18 km frame. With bearings kept, every north-south column must still add up to the world height, so whatever the band gains has to come out of the short strips beyond its ends (Falaknuma, the Cantonment). I tuned four world sizes to the same room targets (in units per real metre):

| world (u) | bearing error p95 / p99 / max | pairs over 15° |
|---|---|---|
| 12000 x 9000 | 13.1 / 16.8 / 21.5° | 55 |
| 14000 x 10500 | 9.5 / 12.6 / 16.1° | 6 |
| **15000 x 11250 (chosen)** | 8.3 / 10.5 / 13.8° | 0 |
| 16000 x 12000 | 7.6 / 9.9 / 13.1° | 0 |

The cost: today's 8000 x 6000 world builds in 774 ms (14,562 structures, about 50 MB heap) on this machine. The chosen size is 3.5x that area, so expect about 2.7 s and 10.5 M collision cells, less if the outskirts get fewer filler blocks. The 12000 x 9000 parameters are kept as a preset if the engine can't afford it, with bearing errors up to 21.5° in the strips south of the Old City and in the Cantonment.

**The warp.** The base projection is uniform (equirectangular about 17.3935 N, 78.448 E, 0.625 u/m). The warp moves each point along the gradient of a smooth bowl-shaped (convex) function, so it never folds, never rotates directions, and maps the frame edges onto the world edges. It is driven by a designed density: background 1 plus one bump per core, a broad plateau and two weak "sinks" that shrink the empty ends of the band. Each bump adds a·(1+d²/s²)^-p:

| kernel | lat | lon | a | s (m) | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| old_city | 17.3625 | 78.4720 | 3.5 | 442 | 0.7 |
| musi | 17.3705 | 78.4785 | 0.905 | 598 | 0.7 |
| abids_koti | 17.3880 | 78.4775 | 1.436 | 684 | 0.9 |
| himayatnagar | 17.4000 | 78.4895 | 1.535 | 442 | 1.1 |
| tank_bund | 17.4165 | 78.4750 | 0.815 | 880 | 1.1 |
| secunderabad | 17.4375 | 78.4980 | 1.148 | 860 | 1.2 |
| plateau | 17.3950 | 78.4820 | 0.668 | 3680 | 0.8 |
| sink_south | 17.3350 | 78.4705 | -0.4 | 1275 | 1.2 |
| sink_north | 17.4680 | 78.4980 | -0.6 | 1246 | 1.0 |

Other settings: gain 0.75, Poisson grid 320 x 240, mean density 1.381.

**Measured at 15000 x 11250:**
- **No fold-overs:** 0 of 210,750 grid triangles flip, the smallest local area factor is 0.62, and the largest rotation is 0.08°.
- **Scale per area:** Charminar 1.15 u/m, Laad Bazaar 1.25, Mecca Masjid 1.17, Chowmahalla 1.08, Madina 1.03, Musi corridor 0.91, Abids 0.98, Koti 0.88, Himayatnagar 0.97, Tank Bund 0.77, Secunderabad Clock Tower 0.77. The outskirts sit at 0.58-0.63 u/m.
- **Bearings:** across 2,167 neighbouring-place pairs the median error is 3.4°, the 99th percentile 10.5° and the worst 13.8°, none over 15°.
- **Order along roads:** 0 inversions in 410 ordered pairs.
- **Footprints:** Mecca Masjid and Chowmahalla need 1.02 u/m with a 12 u gap and get 1.08. Only 1 sizeable overlap remains, Karachi Bakery inside Mozamjahi Market, which is the same spot by design. 26 small prop overlaps need a nudge (listed in the report).
- **Plazas:** a square plaza around Charminar can be up to 136 u half-size before it touches Mecca Masjid.

**The map in the previews** reads as Hyderabad: Hussain Sagar with the Tank Bund and Necklace Road, the Musi with its riverbed and bridges, Mir Alam Tank, Himayat Sagar, both rail lines, and the Old City south of the river.

**Merged places.** places.json has all 651 ids (50 high, 125 medium, 476 low confidence). Each entry records which rule picked the winner and keeps the losing candidate.
notes: How to use it: project(lat, lon) -> [x, y]; unproject(x, y); projectLine / projectRing (they add points every 40 m first, so long straight segments follow the warp); placeWorld(places.json entry); scaleAt(lat, lon) -> {m, upm, mpu, aniso, bearingMaxErr}; inFrame(lat, lon). It loads with require() in node or as window.NOSTALGIA_GEO from a plain <script>. The first call takes about 0.5 s; after that each projection takes about 1 microsecond.

Colony, Ashok Nagar terraces and Patang Chacha's roof: their entries carry anchor_latlon + offset_u and must be placed with placeWorld() = project(anchor) + offset_u, so the roof, plank and stair spacing stays in game units. Their own lat/lon are only the researcher's 2 m/u conversion and must not be projected.

Points outside the frame (KPHB, JNTU, Bolarum, Rashtrapati Nilayam, Ramoji, Harina Vanasthali, University of Hyderabad) project outside the world rectangle by their real distance; clamp them to edge signposts.

The engine is already written against N.WORLD_W / N.WORLD_H. Moving to 15000 x 11250 means changing the constant in src/core.js (I did not touch it; it belongs to the engine team) plus the new worlddata. To stay at 12000 x 9000, use create(PRESETS['12000x9000']) or set PRESET.

places.json tie-breaks when both researchers gave equal confidence: Tank Bund statues and arches follow tank_bund, which the north-west researcher had at high confidence. Sanjeevaiah Park takes the north-west value (the park outline traced on the OSM lake polygon). Two high-confidence values within 150 m are averaged (6 cases, including lumbini_park). Otherwise the candidate inside its game district's polygon wins, then the one citing a data source over a pure estimate, then the researcher who owned that district. hotel_madina, an alias, was moved 214 m onto its target pathergatti.

Rerun order: node tools/geo/merge_places.cjs; node tools/geo/check_projection.cjs --report; node tools/geo/preview.cjs. Optional re-tune: node tools/geo/tune_projection.cjs --preset 15000x11250 (or --world WxH).

The warp is the linearised optimal-transport step described above. I also kept a density-equalising flow mode (Gastner-Seguy-More) in the code; it hits the designed scale exactly, but it added 10.5° of rotation at Charminar, so the gradient mode was chosen.

Credits must include: 'Map reference: DataMeet Municipal Spatial Data (CC BY 4.0) and (c) OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)', plus Overture Maps Foundation, datameet/railways (CC0) and AWS Terrain Tiles (SRTM, public domain). These are recorded in places.json meta and in the report.

The one sizeable overlap, Karachi Bakery inside Mozamjahi Market, is the same spot by design.

map-builder-v2.summary:
The live map (`src/worlddata.js`) is now the real Hyderabad at 15000 x 11250 u. It was generated by the new builder `tools/geo/build_worlddata.cjs` and swapped in with an atomic rename. All checks pass: `validate_map` reports 0 errors, `check_registry` passes (494 registry ids plus all 1,415 ids of the v1 map still exist), the smoke test passes, the seasons test passes, and `tests/map_preview.cjs` renders `tests/out/map_overview.png` and teleports to 42 landmarks in the real engine without errors. The collectibles test does not pass: it has 6 failures caused by v1 coordinates and distances (see known issues).

**What the map is made of**
- **Districts:** the 40 districts are now polygons built from real GHMC wards. Each has `poly`, `polys` and `holes`, plus a bounding `rect` for old code and a gap-free `districtGrid` lookup. world.js already reads both.
- **Roads:** the 214 named roads follow their real alignments. Divided roads get medians, curated roads that cross the Musi get explicit bridge pieces, and the Lower Tank Bund is narrowed and pushed to the foot of the bund. I also added 3,183 residential lanes from an OpenStreetMap extract of Hyderabad that I found already cloned locally. They only go in districts that were built up by 2003, with spacing set per district, and never cross the Musi, a landmark compound or a real park. Every road has a `pothole` hint (0–1) for the pothole work, which world.js already reads.
- **Water:** Hussain Sagar uses its real shoreline with the Buddha's rock as an island. The Musi is a narrow channel inside a sandy riverbed whose width follows the measured widths. The Esi, the nalas and 55 lakes and tanks are included.
- **Rails and terrain:** the railway lines follow real track geometry. Hills and rock fields come from the elevation data, and boulders are scattered in the real rocky areas.
- **Parks:** real shapes for Public Gardens, Lumbini, NTR Gardens, Sanjeevaiah Park, Indira Park, KBR, Parade Grounds, Gymkhana, Gun Park and Victory Playground. The Golconda outer wall runs through the researchers' five estimated wall points, with Fateh Darwaza and Banjara Darwaza as gates.
- **Hand-tuned layouts moved as rigid blocks** (translation only, whole 4 u cells): the Lakshmi Nagar colony with home, terraces, planks, stairs and lanes; the Ashok Nagar terraces; the Charminar plaza (240 u square, ring road redrawn at radius 84 u); Gulzar Houz with the Char Kaman and Patang Chacha's roof; Mecca Masjid; Numaish; LB Stadium; the Qutb Shahi Tombs; the Begumpet apron; Cyber Towers. Approach roads join them along their axes.
- **Landmarks and places:** landmarks sit at their real centres with v1 sizes. Shops and bus stops are snapped to their real street, facing it, then everything is moved off roads, water and other buildings. High-confidence landmarks moved a median of 4 u; estimated ones a median of 32 u. Places stand at their building's entrance on walkable ground. Things outside the frame stand at the map edge where their road leaves it. Stations sit beside the real track and the Tank Bund statues are numbered from the Lumbini end. Respect zones, compounds, avenue trees (49 coconut palms on Necklace Road) and building blocks are regenerated.
- **Confidence:** every place and landmark carries `conf` and `ll` (the lat/lon used).
- **Compatibility aids:** `N.WORLD_DATA.fromV1(x, y)` converts old v1 coordinates (exact inside a moved layout, a local fit elsewhere). Each landmark also keeps its `v1` position for exact landmark-relative conversion. `clusters` lists every rigid translation.

**Cost:** the file is 825 KB. The engine builds the world in 2.0–2.8 s on a quiet machine and 5.6 s was measured under load, with about 35,000 structures and 78 MB of heap. v1 took about 0.8 s.

`design/map_plan.md` is rewritten for v2. It includes the credits line ("Map reference: DataMeet Municipal Spatial Data (CC BY 4.0) and © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)"), a key-coordinates table with lat/lon, confidence, source, world position and local scale, the method, data conventions, story notes with new travel times, and regenerated tables that now include lat/lon and confidence.
notes: How to rebuild: `node tools/geo/build_worlddata.cjs` (about 30 s). It writes `src/.worlddata.next.js`, runs `validate_map` and `check_registry` on it, and renames it over `src/worlddata.js` only if both pass. On errors the live map is left untouched. `--out FILE` builds elsewhere, `--no-swap` validates without swapping, `--verbose` explains every move.

To preview a candidate map without touching the live one: `WORLDDATA=<file> node tests/map_preview.cjs`. The preview serves that file to the engine in place of `src/worlddata.js`. Both validators also accept `--file`.

Extra data source: the OpenStreetMap Hyderabad extract (ODbL) in `/home/user/shivakumar-ui-max/hyderabad-gis-map/Hyd_city_HYD_gis.zip`, already cloned locally. `tools/geo/extract_osm.cjs <unzipped dir>` regenerates `design/geo/osm_streets.json` (2.8 MB) and `design/geo/osm_landuse.json`. The extract only reaches west to lon 78.382, so HITEC City and Gachibowli have named roads only, which also suits 2003.

worlddata.js sets `N.WORLD_W`/`N.WORLD_H` = 15000 x 11250 before world.js loads; core.js keeps 8000 x 6000 only as a default. world.js already reads `poly`/`polys`/`holes`, `districtGrid` and the road `pothole` hint. view3d.js already sizes its chunk grid from `N.WORLD_W`/`N.WORLD_H`.

New fields: landmarks `conf`, `ll`, `v1`, `cluster`, `street`, `track`; places `conf`, `ll`; roads `pothole`, `conf`, `src` ('roads', 'cluster', 'osm', 'grid'), `realName`; water `river`, `nala`; parks `musi_bed` (sandy riverbed), `begumpet_taxiway`, `hill_*`; plus `D.geo` (credits and attribution), `D.clusters`, `D.terrain.hills`, `D.districtGrid` and `D.fromV1()`. Infill lanes, blocks, rocks and trees are packed in the file and unpacked at load in a few ms.

Builder-invented geometry, all marked `conf: 'low'` with a note: `gachibowli_rd` (the Old Mumbai Highway past Gachibowli stadium to the University), the Gandipet road continued west to the frame edge, bridge pieces where `gandipet_rd` and `bapu_ghat_rd` cross the Musi, 11 access spurs (`spur_*`), a connector for the Gandipet island (`gandipet_rd_link`), the Golconda wall curve, the Begumpet runway (09/27 through the airfield reference point) and its taxiway.

world-engine+potholes.summary:
The engine now runs both the v1 map and the live Map v2 (15000 x 11250, which landed during my work), and potholes are in. Every test passes: tests/potholes.cjs (node checks on v1 and v2 plus the real game) and the desktop smoke test on v2. One target is missed: the v2 world build takes 1.26–1.58 s of CPU on a cold start in this sandbox (load average 17–29 on 4 cores), against the < 1.0 s target. The old engine took 2.4 s on the same map. It does meet the target on v1 (0.40–0.46 s) and on v1 stretched to 15000 x 11250 (0.95 s). A warm rebuild of v2 takes 0.43–0.57 s. Wall-clock times in this sandbox are 2–5x the CPU time, so I measured CPU time.

**Engine (src/world.js, src/world_extras.js)**
- **Grid sizing:** every grid and index is sized inside build() from WORLD_DATA.size, which also sets N.WORLD_W/H. Nothing is sized when the script loads any more.
- **Polygon districts:** districts can be polygons, with rect as the fallback. The map builder's exact district raster is used when present (N.world.districtSource = 'grid'). Gaps between polygons go to the nearest district. New helpers: districtLabel, districtPath, districtRings, districtBBox.
- **Map images:** renderMap and the ground painter draw polygon districts. renderMap has a size cap and stamps the scale it actually used on the canvas (canvas.ppu, N.world.mapPPU). The minimap's 0.2 ppu (3000 x 2250 px) is within the cap.
- **Road graph:** it compared every road with every other road; it now uses a spatial index of road segments. On v1 it produces exactly the same graph as before.
- **Allocation cuts:** the map fills, the nearest-road lookup and the lot generation do less work and allocate less. Rooftop items on buildings and tree canopies are now built only when first drawn (lots and buildings are unchanged on v1).
- **Chunk cache:** render.js was not edited and the chunk cache is unchanged.
- **world_extras.js:** rail data is re-measured on every build. The over-water test reads the surface grid. Level crossings are filtered by bounding box first. The rail overlay on the map uses the map's actual scale.

**Potholes (A2)**
- **Placement:** fixed per road segment (the random seed is road id + segment index). Density depends on road kind and district, and v2's per-road `pothole` hint is used. Sizes are 3–9 u. On v2, per 100 u of road: Old City lanes 2.05, colony lanes 1.72, arterials 0.37, Tank Bund 0.18, HITEC roads 0.03.
- **Exclusions:** none on bridges or within 26 u of a bridge end, none on zebra crossings, near level crossings or overlapping. Junctions where only lanes meet have no zebras, so potholes may come close to those.
- **Monsoon / rain:** more potholes appear (+45%), and in rain they fill with water. These extra potholes are generated the first time they are needed and never change the dry set.
- **Off the boot path:** potholes are generated about 3 ms per frame after the build, and potholeAt returns null until then. On v2 this is 11,376 potholes and 2,308 tar patches, about 0.7 s of work over 52–65 frames on the title screen.
- **API:** `N.world.potholeAt(x, y)` returns `{depth, r, wet, …}` or null and takes 0.05–0.5 µs per call. `N.world.potholes` has the full list, a list per 256 u chunk, `query()` for any rectangle (for 3D), plus `ready`, `ensure()` and the event `potholes:change`.
- **2D look:** a ragged dark hole with a lighter crumbled edge, a sunlit floor, gravel and cracks, plus tar patches. Water in wet potholes is drawn live and reflects the sky colour for the time of day, with rain ripples (about 0.4 ms per frame).
- **Vehicles:** vehicles.js already calls potholeAt. In the test a cycle ridden through a pothole fired `vehicle:pothole`.

**ARCHITECTURE.md** now covers the world size coming from the data, the Map v2 data format, polygon districts and the build-speed notes (§4 and §7). There is a new §7 "Potholes" subsection with the vehicles snippet you specified (×0.82 speed, shake 1.5, 'pothole' sound, 4% cycle puncture, 2% fall above 80% speed), and §14 lists the new test.

**Things for other owners**
- **tests/engine_qa.cjs** has 10 failures:
  - 'N constants' still checks for 8000 x 6000.
  - The two boat tests pick the water shape with the most points, which on v2 is a narrow river, so they find no spot.
  - The other 7 failures (dateLabel base, input actions, four mission-cleanup leaks, midnight clock wrap) do not involve world.js.
- **menus.js** (full map) colours, outlines and labels districts using `d.rect`. On v2 those rects overlap; it should use districtPath / districtLabel.
- **hud.js** makes its own copy of the 3000 x 2250 map image, so the minimap holds two of them. It could ask for 0.12 ppu or read canvas.ppu.
- **render.js** stores chunk indices in a way that allows at most 64 chunk columns or rows (16,384 u). 15000 u needs 59.
- **core.js** 8000/6000, seasons.js `|| 8000` and view3d.js `8000/6000` are fallbacks only; view3d already resizes itself from the real world size.

**To get v2 under 1.0 s:** the map builder could use fewer outskirts filler blocks (24.7k lots today), and avenue and park trees could be built over the first frames like the potholes are. The real-geometry data and its coordinates are the map builder's. I added no geodata myself.
notes: Run the test with: node nostalgia/tests/potholes.cjs. Options: ONLY=node|browser; DATA=path to test another map file (for example a builder candidate); BIG=1 adds the v1 map stretched to 15000 x 11250 as a stress test. The node part builds each map in its own process and uses CPU time, so the numbers do not depend on machine load.

Results: potholes PASSED on v2, on v1 and in the browser. The desktop smoke test PASSED on v2 (boot about 6 s wall under load, world build 2.4 s wall). The 3D view (tps) runs with the new world and potholes in rain, with no errors.
The v1 map is read from design/geo/worlddata_v1.js, a copy the map builder keeps. Both maps pass every pothole and district check.

The map builder's district format is used as written: rect (bounding box) + poly + polys (every ring, the main one included) + holes, plus the exact districtGrid. The road `pothole` field (0..1 hint) scales density but cannot lift a low district much, so HITEC stays near zero.
The 'potholes' system has order 6 and runs in every mode. It polls the weather every 0.5 s and also listens to weather / season:change / calendar:change / game:new / save:loaded.
When the set of potholes changes, R.shadowEpoch is bumped so cached chunks repaint one per frame without blank frames. In 3D, invalidateChunks() is called instead.
Potholes are never drawn or reported on rooftops: potholeAt returns null while the roof grid is in use.

Profiling aids: N.world.buildPhases, N.world.graphPhases, N.world.potholes.stats (counts per kind / style / district, reasons for rejection, work ms, frames) and N.world.potholes.rebuild() after tuning N.world.POTHOLE.

About 25% of the cold build is garbage collection from the roughly 35k structures and 14.6k road nodes. Potholes are not included (they come after the build). v1 (0.40-0.46 s) and v1 stretched to 15000 x 11250 (0.95 s) are within the target. Next steps: fewer filler blocks in the outskirts (map builder) and building trees over the first frames like potholes.

The other 7 (dateLabel base, input actions, four mission-cleanup leaks, midnight clock wrap) do not involve world.js.
menus.js full map draws district tints, borders and names from d.rect. On v2 those are overlapping bounding boxes; it should switch to N.world.districtPath / districtLabel.
hud.js copies the 0.2 ppu map image (3000 x 2250 px on v2), so two such canvases are in memory. It could ask for 0.12 ppu or use canvas.ppu.

The player's v2 home spawn reports SOLID at 10102,4984 in the smoke test. The same thing happened on v1 with the original world.js, so it predates my changes (map data or story placement).

geo-verifier.summary:
I checked the new map against the real city: 1,340 relations now pass at 98.8 %, up from 97.8 %, and it reads as Hyderabad. The pass rate and every result are in `design/geo/verify_report.md`. The new map is live (atomic swap), and `validate_map` and `check_registry` both pass. The one real distortion left is that the middle of the city is stretched east-west, which I diagnosed but did not fix.

**Pass rates (before / old map against corrected data / after)**

| check | before | old map, corrected data | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| compass sector between pairs | 187/193 | 185/191 | 187/191 |
| which place is closer | 103/109 | 108/109 | 108/109 |
| order along roads (incl. Tank Bund statues, Old City spine) | 114/115 | 114/115 | 114/115 |
| Musi crossings, west to east | 22/22 | 22/22 | 22/22 |
| stations along each line | 50/50 | 50/50 | 50/50 |
| which bank of the Musi | 167/167 | 167/167 | 167/167 |
| district (ward) | 463/472 | 464/472 | 465/472 |
| road follows its real line | 182/184 | 182/184 | 182/184 |
| city structure (lake, Tank Bund, Necklace Road, Musi, edges) | 25/30 | 25/30 | 29/30 |
| **all** | **97.8 %** | **98.3 %** | **98.8 %** |

The relations are generated from the real lat/lon in `places.json`, `roads.json`, `water.json`, `rail.json` and `districts.json`. They are tested on the positions the builder actually wrote, after its moves and nudges.

**How the brief's points come out** (real bearing → map bearing)
- **Old City:** Charminar sits in its own district. Laad Bazaar is west (279° → 279°), Mecca Masjid south-west (232° → 235°), Gulzar Houz north.
- **Musi:** it crosses the map west to east, between Charminar and Abids/Koti. Its 11 crossings are in the right order, Gandipet Road to Nagole.
- **Hussain Sagar:** the Buddha is on his island in the south-central part of the lake. Tank Bund runs SSW–NNE (31°; 37° in the map) with the lake on its north-west side. Necklace Road wraps the west and south shore.
- **Koti, Abids, Nampally:** all in the right places.
- **Secunderabad:** the Clock Tower is north-east of the lake (54° → 58°).
- **Begumpet airport:** it is actually due north of the lake (352°), not north-west as the brief says. The map has it at 354°.
- **Outskirts:** Golconda is west (287° → 290°), Cyber Towers north-west of Charminar (315° → 316°), and Dilsukhnagar south-east of the lake (138° → 137°).

**What I fixed**
- **Pathergatti and the Madina Building** stood about 150 m west of Pathergatti Road. I took their positions from the OpenStreetMap road. The `pathergatti` place now stands at the stone arcades, which is where cassette 9's hint puts it. The Madina Building is now at Madina circle (`hotel_madina` follows it). Both moved 250–310 u.
- **Bridge and Lower Tank Bund coordinates were wrong in the data, not the map.** Naya Pul, the Salar Jung bridge, Musallam Jung and Chaderghat were 135–410 m off in `places.json`; the builder had already placed them on the real bridges. I replaced them with the OpenStreetMap bridge midpoints. The Lower Tank Bund point was 180 m east of its road; I moved it onto the road, which needed no map change.
- **Builder bugs on the Gandipet road:**
  - Four "To …" signposts (Gandipet, Chilkur Balaji, Mrugavani, Himayat Sagar) stood 4 km inside the map. They now stand at the west edge.
  - The road's estimated part ran along the river as one 3.6 km "bridge". It now keeps to the south bank and has a single short bridge.
- **The fixes survive a re-merge.** They live in `places_fixes.json`, and `merge_places.cjs` now applies them as its last step.

regression.summary:
I ran the full regression pass against Map v2. I found and fixed one serious map-caused regression: about 2,000 road ends stopped just short of the road they meet, so routes made long detours. The fix is now in the live map.

**State of the live map:** `src/worlddata.js` (swapped at 15:49) passes `validate_map` with 0 errors and `check_registry`. Every place can be reached on foot from home except the Buddha statue, which is reached by boat, as in v1. The new route check passes.

**1. Map-caused regression, fixed (generator)**
- **The problem:** the engine only joins a road end that lies within the other road's w/2+6. 2,396 road ends were dead ends in `N.world.roads`, most of them 5–40 u short of a road. The Afzalgunj, Musallam Jung and Purana Pul bridges each dead-ended on one bank.
- **Effect on routes:** the median detour of 400 random routes was 1.44x (v1: 1.23x), and the 90th percentile was 2.18x. Koti→Charminar was 1.88x, Charminar→Golconda 2.14x, home→Secunderabad 1.91x.
- **The fix:** the new `tools/geo/near_miss.cjs` is called from a short hook at step 9.76 of the builder. It runs after landmarks are placed, so no landmark moves, and joins 1,182 ends with short connectors. Connectors never cross water, solid buildings, rails, roof zones or the Musi bed (bridges excepted), and OSM lanes stay out of the no-infill zones.
- **Result:** median detour 1.27x, 90th percentile 1.50x. Koti→Charminar 1.50x (now via Afzalgunj, Naya Pul and Pathergatti), Charminar→Golconda 1.29x, home→Secunderabad 1.44x. Dead-end warnings dropped from 2,382 to 1,084; most of the rest are tails past a junction or real cul-de-sacs.
- **Guard against regressions:** the new `tools/geo/route_check.cjs` builds the real engine world in node and checks the detours. It passes on the live map and fails on the pre-fix map.
- **How it went live:** a geography-verification agent was editing `build_worlddata.cjs`, `project.cjs` and `places*.json` at the same time. Its rebuild at 15:49 included my pass, and the live map is byte-identical to the candidate I validated. I did not swap the map myself.

**2. world.js (additive only)**
- `N.world.roads.route(a, b, {walk, costs, avoid, paths, maxExpand})` is an A* with a binary heap and reused typed arrays. It matches a reference A* on 60 random pairs, and home→Charminar takes 5.6 ms in the browser under load. `routeStats()` returns `{expanded, len}`.
- `N.world.renderMap(ppu, {fresh: true})` returns an uncached canvas, so the HUD can grade it in place instead of keeping a second 27 MB copy.
- The potholes node checks pass on v1 and v2. In the desktop smoke test, boot, teleports and console errors are fine; the walk check failed at 5 fps under load.

**3. Test results (v2, then the same snapshot with the v1 map as a baseline)**

Load average was 25–65 on 4 cores throughout, so many timing checks are flaky.

| Result | Suites |
|---|---|
| Pass | smoke (first run), seasons, landmarks_gallery, places_gallery, map_preview, validate_map, check_registry. story_part2 passed 61/61 in the story agent's own run on v2. |
| Map-caused, other owners | menus (tests use v1 Charminar coordinates; boot over 20 s), engine_qa (8000×6000 assertion; 2 boat tests), collectibles (C13, G24, C10), npcs (fixed time budgets for routes that are now 1.7–2.3x longer). |
| Not map-caused (same failure on v1, or isolated) | core_systems, audio, engine_qa dist build: PLAY now starts the prologue cutscene and the tests wait for 'play'. With a local skip patch, the remaining failures come from vehicle rules (A3) and the removed DEMO mission, and are identical on v1. Also engine_qa's other contract/bugs failures (on v1 too), storycore, shops, traffic, cricket_match, minigames, vehicles_v2, potholes cycle ride, view3d, and the view3d_actors gait check (3D agent working on it). |
| Probably not the map, not proven | story_part1 on v2 got stuck in a walkman dialogue in M6, then cascaded. It was not run on v1. |

The HUD GPS problem is map-caused but has no test: confirmed in the game, Charminar→Cyber Towers and LB Nagar→Cyber Towers fall back to a straight line. The A* in hud.js stops after 6,000 expanded nodes, and these trips need about 7,000 and 8,400.

**4. Performance on the bigger world**
- **World build:** 1.45–1.52 s CPU cold and 1.0–1.15 s warm in node, against 0.52 s for v1 and a 1.0 s target. My joins did not add cost (the pre-fix map took 1.54–1.57 s). In the browser the cold build was 2.9 s, with garbage collection about 31% of boot CPU; under load it reaches about 6.2 s and boot about 15 s (v1: 7 s). I did not fix this: it needs blocks generated over the first frames, or fewer outskirts lots in the builder (24.7k lots, e.g. Tolichowki 1,930).
- **Frame cost:** no regression. Canvas calls per frame at the same places are equal to or lower than v1 (Charminar 17.0k vs 18.9k; Abids 14.2k vs 18.5k; densest window 13.5k vs 19.1k). Sampled busy time at Abids at night was 24.4 ms on v2 vs 26.0 ms on v1 under the same load.
- **Memory:** JS heap after garbage collection is 38.8 MB at the title (v1 15.9) and 48.7 MB in play (v1 26.9). The minimap image takes 27 MB, held twice.

**5. Patches for other owners**
- **hud.js:** at line 244 use `R.route(a, b, {walk: true, paths: true, costs: {path: 1.15}})`. In `mapImage`, use `renderMap(MM.ppu, {fresh: true})` and grade it in place.
- **vehicles.js** (lines 2869–2900, limit 8,000, linear open list) and **wanted.js** (line 852, limit 6,000): call `N.world.roads.route(..., {walk: true})`.
- **collectibles.js:**
  - Line 263: use `fromV1(4585, 2649)`, which gives [10113, 4989]. The v1 coordinate falls back to the stair foot and takes over the stairs' ACTION.
  - Line 370: Bala Hissar radius should be at least 1,500 (G24 is 1,366 u away on v2, 562 on v1).
  - C10: the `abids_book_market` anchor sits in the middle of the road; add an offset, or allow 30 u.
- **engine_qa.cjs:**
  - Line 68: compare against `WORLD_DATA.size`.
  - Line 394: pick `water.find(w => w.id === 'hussain_sagar')`; I verified this works on v2.
- **core_systems.cjs** (lines 77, 460, 523), **audio.cjs** (line 80), **engine_qa.cjs** (line 906): after PLAY, click `.cs-skip` if the mode is 'cutscene'.
- **menus.cjs:** lines 90, 192 and 205 should use `N.places.charminar` (plus the same offsets); raise the line 68 boot timeout to 60 s.
- **npcs.cjs:** scale the time budgets by path length.
- **menus.js** (lines 1509–1514, 1552, 1586–1594): use `districtPath`/`districtLabel`/`districtBBox`, and size the grid-reference loops from the world size.
- **seasons.js** (lines 1295, 1340, 1414–1419): use `fromV1()` — e.g. [3936,4020]→[9123,7782], the Laad Bazaar strip → 8525–8929 × 8218–8251 — or anchor to places.
- **places_art.js** (lines 2269–2273, 2369, 2418): add `lm.x - lm.v1[0]` and `lm.y - lm.v1[1]`. This is exact, because the face and size are unchanged.
- **story2.js** (lines 2504, 2817) and **shops.js** (line 2060): `randomRoute(n, 5–6)` now covers 3–5x less distance on the denser graph; use more steps.
- **All tests:** raise 20 s boot timeouts to 60 s.
